subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should the shared auth-profile manager retry only explicitly classified transient OAuth refresh failures, and what total retry latency is acceptable while the cross-agent refresh lock is held?
rationale: The current manager intentionally serializes refreshes and bounds one call; choosing which provider errors are safe to repeat and how long peers may wait changes shared auth behavior across built-in and plugin-owned providers.

options.title: Adopt classified bounded retries
options.body: Retry only a small, documented set of transport and transient upstream failures within a lock-safe total budget, while preserving immediate propagation for terminal OAuth errors.

options.title: Keep one-shot refreshes
options.body: Retain the current timeout, lock, adoption, and rotating-token recovery paths without generic retry behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt classified bounded retries
recommendation.body: Retry only a small, documented set of transport and transient upstream failures within a lock-safe total budget, while preserving immediate propagation for terminal OAuth errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing serialization and timeout invariants were introduced in this auth-refresh path by this contributor.
